subject: anatomy
title: Heart, pericardium and coronary circulation: key anatomy for exams

steps.tx: The heart sits in the middle mediastinum inside the **pericardium**, a two-layered sac. The tough outer layer is the **fibrous pericardium**. The inner **serous pericardium** has a parietal layer lining the fibrous sac and a visceral layer (epicardium) fused to the heart. Pain-sensitive structures are the fibrous and parietal layers, supplied by the phrenic nerve. The visceral layer is pain-insensitive, supplied by autonomic nerves.

steps.tx: The **right atrium** receives the SVC, IVC and coronary sinus. Its inner wall has the **crista terminalis**, a muscular ridge separating the smooth sinus venarum from the trabeculated appendage. The **Koch's triangle** lies between the tendon of Todaro, the septal tricuspid cusp and the coronary sinus opening. The AV node sits at its apex, and the **SA node** lies at the upper crista terminalis near the SVC.

steps.tx: The **coronary sinus** is the largest cardiac vein. It lies in the posterior part of the coronary sulcus and opens into the right atrium, guarded by the incomplete Thebesian valve. Its tributaries are the great, middle and small cardiac veins, the posterior vein of the left ventricle, the oblique vein of the left atrium and the right marginal vein. The anterior cardiac veins and venae cordis minimi drain directly into the chambers.

steps.tx: Coronary **dominance** depends on which artery gives the posterior interventricular branch. In **right dominance**, seen in about 67 to 90 percent of people, the right coronary artery gives it. In **left dominance**, seen in about 10 to 15 percent, the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery gives it. The left coronary artery arises from the left posterior aortic sinus and supplies more tissue overall.

steps.tx: Trace **atrial septation** in four stages. **Septum primum** grows down, holes form the **foramen secundum**, and septum secundum grows on the right-atrial side. The primum stays on as the flap of the **foramen ovale** until birth. The second schematic marks where ASD, VSD and PDA occur.
